7612.t: Assumed to be from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁- (“to perceive, pay attention”) and therefore related to κοέω (koéō), Latin caveō, Sanskrit कवि (kaví, “wise, poet, seer, sage”), Persian کی (kay, “poet-king”), Lithuanian kavoti (“safeguard, tend”), Old…

7669.t: Likely from Pre-Greek because of the presence of -αλλ- (-all-).

7601.t: According to Beekes, from a Proto-Indo-European *ḱerd- (“craft, cunning”) and cognate with Old Irish cerd (“craft, skill”) (< *ḱerd-h₂-), Welsh cerdd (“song”).

7661.t: Traditionally taken to be from an earlier *λέχ-σκα (*lékh-skā) with metathesis of the -σ- (-s-), a nominal formation from the same root as λέχομαι (lékhomai, “to recline”) and λέχος n (lékhos, “bed”).

7617.t: According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leh₁g- (“weak, faint”), the same root of λαγαρός (lagarós, “hollow, sunken”), λαγαίω (lagaíō, “to release”), λάγνος (lágnos, “lascivious”), λήγω (lḗgō, “to stop, cease”), and λωγάνιον (lōgánion, “dewlap of…

7611.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kṓpā, from Proto-Indo-European *kóh₂p-eh₂, from the root *keh₂p- (“to seize, grab”), which also gives κάπτω (káptō, “gulp down”).

7600.t: Unknown. Has long been compared to κεράννυμι (keránnumi, “to mix”), but could also be related to Latin cremō, Proto-West Germanic *herþ (English hearth), or Sanskrit कूडयति (kūḍayati, “to burn, scorch”).

7688.t: Traditionally compared with Latin mandō (“to chew”) (< Proto-Indo-European *meth₂-) and Proto-Germanic *munþaz (“mouth”) (< *mn̥t-), assuming the original form of the Greek term's root as μαθ- (math-), though unresolved phonetic issues with the above lead…

7635.t: From λείπω (leípō, “to leave, to quit”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

7664.t: From Proto-Hellenic *lāros, from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂- (expressive root). Cognate with Latin lātrō, Latin lamentum, λάλος (lálos), λάσκω (láskō).

7604.t: The formation is like other plant names, such as μάνυζα (mánuza), μώλυζα (mṓluza) and ὄρυζα (óruza). The assumption that it was formed from κονίς (konís, “nit”) is unwarranted.

7668.t: Almost certainly a technical word of Pre-Greek origin, because of the many different variants.

7667.t: As for its accent, this word agrees with secondary adjectives like χρύσεος (khrúseos), λίθεος (lítheos), βόεος (bóeos), but conceptually it rather belongs to primary oxytones, like ἐτεός (eteós), κενεός (keneós), στερεός (stereós).

7616.t: Unexplained. Connection with Latin lāma (“marsh, mud”) and Lithuanian lōmas (“pit, hollow”) is semantically unconvincing.

7653.t: From λυσι- (lusi-, “loosing, releasing”), from λύω (lúō) + -τελής (-telḗs), from τέλος (télos, “end, completion; here: dues”).

7641.t: From λιμός (limós) + κτείνω (kteínō), equivalent to λιμοκτόνος (limoktónos) + -έω (-éō).
